description:
Running work fits agent-first work previews to the available width. The test seeded a conversation at /c/rw-previews; the browser is told (through rewritten responses, with live updates cut off) that it has three idle subagents, "demo-index", "demo-assets" and "demo-build", each running one background job "printf preview-ready; tail -f /dev/null". "The toggle" is [data-testid="running-work-toggle"]. "The names" are the texts of the toggle's ".running-work-name" elements, in order, whitespace collapsed: eval `JSON.stringify([...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="running-work-toggle"] .running-work-name')].map(e => e.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()))`. "The overflow" is scrollWidth - clientWidth of the toggle's ".running-work-names".
1. Navigate to /c/rw-previews.
2. The names should be exactly ["demo-index","demo-assets"]. The toggle's ".running-work-more" should have exactly the text "and 4 more", and the toggle should contain "3 tasks · 3 subagents".
3. Set the viewport to 1600x900. The names should become exactly ["demo-index","demo-assets","demo-build","printf preview-ready; tail -f /dev/null","printf preview-ready; tail -f /dev/null","printf preview-ready; tail -f /dev/null"], and there should be no ".running-work-more" in the toggle (count 0). The overflow should become at most 1.
4. Set the viewport to 390x700. The names should become exactly ["demo-index","demo-assets"] again, the toggle's ".running-work-more" exactly "and 4 more", and the overflow should become at most 1.
